title: X-ray
look: A security scanner image: translucent orange and blue layers on black, every inner part showing through, on a belt.

doc.essence: The character passing through a baggage scanner: soft parts read as see-through orange, harder parts as blue, and wherever parts overlap the image gets denser, so you see right into it.
doc.notIt: Not glass (dark scanner field, two material colours, no blobs), not hologram (two hues by density, a belt not a HUD, no scan lines), not blueprint (translucent fills, no grid).
doc.shapes: Every part has a dense bright rim and a translucent inside, so overlapping parts and their edges all show.
doc.colour: Body and belly in organic orange, darker and harder parts in metal blue, all translucent over near-black.
doc.eyes: Near-white: the densest thing in the scan.
pitfalls: Overlaps add up to opaque: keep the fill opacities low.
The palette only decides which parts are 'metal': colours themselves are not kept.
